observation_summary: The unescape method incorrectly attempts to convert numeric XML entities that exceed the maximum character value (0xFFFF) into characters, resulting in incorrect output instead of leaving the entity string as-is.
hypothesis: The code lacks a validation check to ensure that the parsed numeric entity value is within the valid range for a character (0xFFFF). When the value exceeds this, it is incorrectly processed as a valid character.
prediction: Adding a check to verify if the parsed entityValue is greater than 0xFFFF and setting it to -1 (indicating an invalid entity) will cause the unescape logic to correctly treat the input as a literal string rather than an invalid character.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the addition of 'if (entityValue > 0xFFFF) { entityValue = -1; }' in both the string and writer-based unescape methods, confirming that the root cause was a missing boundary check for the numeric entity value.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic missing boundary check. The code parses a numeric entity but fails to validate if the resulting integer is a valid character code. Adding this check prevents the overflow/invalid character conversion, which is the definition of a Checking defect.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves code changes, the core issue is the absence of a guard condition (validation) for the parsed value, which is the hallmark of a Checking defect.
